name: Silk-TS-TW

frames.best_why: A broad satin fold sweeps corner to corner with the strongest light and shadow contrast.

tagline: Folds of grey silk ripple slowly across the whole screen.
summary: A full-screen shader paints soft diagonal folds of grey-lilac silk that drift and bend without end. It turns an empty section into a textured, fabric-like backdrop.
appearance: The whole stage is filled with grey-lilac cloth that looks like folded silk, soft diagonal bands running corner to corner. Highlights form pale ribbons while deep creases fall into near-black shadow.
behaviour: The folds slide slowly sideways, bright ribbons and shadows crossing one another. The motion never stops, so the fabric keeps a gentle breathing rhythm.
demo_content: Full-bleed grey-lilac silk at default speed, scale and rotation.
search_phrases: slow moving fabric for a hero
cloth folds behind a landing page
use_when: A quiet, premium section wants a moving textile texture behind its content.
avoid_when: The palette is a single flat grey, and its constant movement can distract from dense copy.
customise: Speed, scale, base colour, noise and rotation are props; the wave shape itself lives in the shader and needs source editing.
weight_why: A three.js canvas re-renders a shader plane every frame.

a11y.note: A canvas backdrop with nothing to label; the endless motion ignores reduced-motion settings.

polish_why: Convincing silk folds with smooth, slow motion; the grey palette is flat and bands can blur.
title: Silk
